rule: Daily carbohydrate by tier: high 5.5, moderate 4.0, low 3.0 g/kg (scaled down proportionally when MacroFactor's weekly total can't fund them)
summary: The ACSM/AND/DC 2016 tiers are 3-5 g/kg for light days, 5-7 for a moderate program (~1 h/day) and 6-10 for 1-3 h/day of moderate-to-high work. The ISSN puts 2-3 h/day of intense training at 5-8 g/kg. Low (3) and moderate (4) sit inside the light band. High (5.5) is at the bottom of the moderate band, which fits ~1-1.5 h/day of concurrent training. Strength-training evidence shows little carbohydrate dose-response, while CrossFit-style training seems to benefit from higher-carb diets. These are directional ranges, not tested numbers. Their real effect is limited because they only redistribute MacroFactor's total: at the current 2834 kcal the average is ~4 g/kg. Revisit only if long-run or Hyrox weeks run above ~2 h/day.

sources.note: Joint position stand on athlete nutrition (abstract); its carbohydrate table (seen via search reproduction) gives light 3-5, moderate ~1 h/day 5-7, 1-3 h/day 6-10, extreme 8-12 g/kg/day
ISSN 2018: general fitness 3-5 g/kg; 2-3 h/day intense training 5-8 g/kg; 3-6 h/day 8-10 g/kg
Burke 2011: judge carbohydrate by whether availability matches the day's training demand
Henselmans 2022 SR (49 studies): no dose-response of carbohydrate on strength performance; benefit mainly with fasted controls or >10 sets per muscle
CrossFit scoping review: athletes under-eat carbohydrate; high-carb diets helped CrossFit performance
